context:
Simple parameter change in tuning.py. Check the max_bytes_in_join calculation
and restore to 50% multiplier. Then grep for join_algorithm across the ClickHouse
adapter to verify grace_hash isn't overridden by session-level settings.
description:
ClickHouse SF1 Q5 fails across TPC-H, tpchavoc, and tpch_skew with:
"Limit for JOIN exceeded, max bytes: 2.00 GiB, current bytes: 2.72 GiB"

Root cause: benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/tuning.py ~line 91 sets max_bytes_in_join
to 25% of max_memory_usage. With a 2 GB default, that's 512 MB - too low for Q5's
multi-table join at SF1 which needs 2.72 GB.

Additionally, join_algorithm should be set to "grace_hash" (~line 105) which spills
to disk and should avoid this limit entirely. Need to verify grace_hash is actually
taking effect and not being overridden.

Single fix resolves 9 failures across 3 benchmarks.

anti_patterns.why: SF1 Q5 multi-table join needs 2.72 GiB and 25% cap caused OOM
grace_hash spills to disk and is the safety net when memory limits are hit

preserves.behavior: All other tuning parameters (max_memory_usage, max_threads, etc.) retain current values
Tuning applies correctly for both SF0.01 and SF1 scales
grace_hash join algorithm setting is not overridden by adapter session defaults

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/ -v -k 'clickhouse and tuning and (join or memory)'
verifications.description: Tuning tests pass with updated max_bytes_in_join multiplier
verifications.expected: Tests pass confirming 0.5 multiplier and grace_hash settings
